text: The theory of groups over the signature (·, ⁻¹, e) consists of universally quantified equations. Which property is NOT one of the group axioms (G1–G3)?
choices: Identity: e·x = x and x·e = x
Inverses: x⁻¹·x = e and x·x⁻¹ = e
explanation: The three group axioms are associativity (G1), the identity laws (G2), and the inverse laws (G3); commutativity is not required. A group that additionally satisfies x·y = y·x is called abelian, so commutativity is an extra property, not part of the definition of a group.
